8月17日是印尼獨立81周年，多個在港印尼人團體今（23日）在銅鑼灣維園舉行慶祝活動，吸引眾多外傭參與，穿著傳統民俗服飾載歌載舞。同場有多個機構提供中醫、按摩、手工藝攤位，主辦單位指外傭作為香港家庭的照顧者，冀藉活動關懷他們的身心健康。

印尼獨立81周年，多個在港印尼人團體今（23日）在銅鑼灣維園舉行慶祝活動，吸引眾多外傭參與，穿著傳統民俗服飾載歌載舞。同場有多個機構提供中西醫、按摩、手工藝攤位，主辦單位指外傭作為香港家庭的照顧者，冀藉活動關懷他們的身心健康。

Indonesia gained independence in 1945 after more than 300 years of Dutch colonial rule, with August 17 marked as Independence Day, an important local holiday. Hong Kong is home to over 160,000 Indonesian domestic workers. The Mission for Migrant Workers (MFMW), the Indonesian Migrant Workers Network (JBMI) and the Indonesian Migrant Workers Union (IMWU) have organised Independence Day celebrations every August for many years to bring together members of the Indonesian domestic worker community who are far from home.

印傭穿民俗服飾同歡 暫忘壓力

This year's event was again held at Victoria Park. Siti, who has been working in Hong Kong for seven years, said most of those attending were domestic workers who faced heavy daily pressures and were unable to celebrate on Independence Day itself. She was therefore glad to have the chance to gather together and enjoy a joyful time like back home. Siti turned up today wearing traditional Balinese dress, while Via, a fellow domestic worker beside her, dressed up as Srikandi, a female warrior from East Javanese mythology representing beauty and strength combined, attracting many to take photos.

本地及印尼團體設攤供義務醫療

The performance stage naturally drew the crowds, while the on-site massage, health check and eye examination booths also had long queues. Volunteer masseuse Tini said they learnt massage skills in their spare time and took the chance to practise while serving the community, easing the shoulder, back and head pain that domestic workers often suffer from over the long term.

主辦次一 MFMW 的社區關係主任唐曉昕表示，中心平時接觸的外傭求助個案多與其工作相關，然而外傭亦非常缺乏日常身心照顧，希望藉嘉年華活動提供「Care for Caregiver」的服務，多年來獲得不少本地醫療界人士支持。

外傭難言病痛「唔想被覺得好難搞」

She explained that although labour laws guarantee domestic workers access to medical resources provided by employers, and some employers welcome their workers raising health needs proactively, many domestic workers are reluctant to speak up for fear of being seen as 'difficult to deal with, as it is hard to judge what is appropriate'. The centre hopes the event will help domestic workers gain access to self-care opportunities and information, while creating moments for them to care for one another, so that even while far from home they can be supported by a friendly community.

續跟進宏福苑歷劫外傭個案

Today also saw the participation of domestic workers affected by the deadly fire at Wang Fuk Court. Tang Hiu-yan said those who went through the ordeal still face various difficulties, such as having to travel across districts daily to care for elderly employers who live with them or reside in care homes in Tai Po, or looking after elders who developed emotional problems after the fire. Some domestic workers have also suffered mental distress bordering on depression, though fortunately some understanding employers have agreed to terminate their contracts so they could return home to recuperate. The MFMW will continue to provide support for affected domestic workers and follow up on cases in need.
